originalTitle: Why IBM shares crashed 26%: CEO Arvind Krishna highlights customer spending shifts towards AI
simplifiedContent: IBM's stock price dropped by 26% because the company's recent financial results were not as good as expected. The main reason for this is that customers are changing how they spend their money, and they are now prioritizing artificial intelligence (AI) technology. This shift in spending, along with some mistakes made by the company and a slowdown in its mainframe business, led to the poor results. As a result, the company's stock price fell sharply, which is a big deal for investors who own IBM shares. This matters because it shows that IBM is facing challenges in keeping up with changes in what its customers want to buy.

originalTitle: Fed's Warsh vows to 'do my job' if challenged by Trump
simplifiedContent: The head of the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, said he will do his job to control inflation, even if the President tries to influence him. This means he will make decisions based on what's best for the economy, not on what politicians want. Inflation, or the rate at which prices rise, went down a bit in June, but Warsh doesn't plan to cut interest rates right now. This decision affects the stock market, where investors are now less likely to expect interest rate increases soon. Warsh's goal is to keep prices stable, which is important for the overall health of the economy.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market went down on a particular day because of increasing tensions in West Asia. This led to higher crude oil prices and a weaker rupee, which made people worry about inflation. As a result, two important stock market measures, Sensex and Nifty, decreased by up to 0.7%. Despite some positive news about company earnings, the concerns about global politics had a bigger impact on the market. This means that investors are more focused on the potential risks from global events than on the good news from companies.

originalTitle: Multibagger Signature Global shares to be in focus on Wednesday after Q1 pre-sales rise 25% QoQ
simplifiedContent: Signature Global, a company listed on the stock market, will be closely watched on Wednesday due to its recent sales update. The company's sales for the first quarter of the financial year 2027 were ₹1,970 crore, which is 25% lower than the same time last year, but 25% higher than the previous quarter. This increase is partly because of a new project called Tonino Lamborghini Residences. This news matters because it shows how the company's sales are doing, which can affect its stock price. Investors will be paying attention to see how the market reacts to this update on Wednesday.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver rebound as softer US inflation eases Fed rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: The prices of gold and silver went up on July 14th because of some good news about inflation in the US. Inflation, which is the rate at which prices are rising, was lower than expected, which means the US central bank (called the Fed) might not raise interest rates as much as people thought. This is good for gold and silver, so their prices rose - gold went up to $4,112 and silver went up to $60. This change in inflation also helped because people were worried that the Fed would raise interest rates, which would have made it more expensive to borrow money. As a result, investors felt more confident in buying gold and silver.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and a company called LIC are planning to sell a big portion of their shares in IDBI Bank. Together, they own almost 95% of the bank, and they want to sell about 60.72% of it. This sale would not only give them money, but also mean they would no longer be in charge of the bank. The government and LIC are currently reviewing new offers from potential buyers, which means the process of selling their shares is moving forward. This matters because it would be a significant change in who owns and controls IDBI Bank.
